How the film industry blew it with 3D

I would go so far as to say that the failure of 3D is entirely due to the surcharges. People have been watching bad movies, and movies with a few bad moments, for over a century. They have been watching other bad entertainments for millennia. People go to the movies expecting to be entertained. If the price of admission is half again as high people expect the entertainment to be half again as good, and 3D just is not that much of an improvement of the entertainment experience.

People already regard going to movies as being an expensive venture, especially if you get drinks/snacks from their concessions. But when you add a $2-$5 surcharge to see a film in 3D versus the regular showing, some people will simply go see the 2D version.

Personally, I'm a fan of 3D movies, especially if a film I'm interested in seeing is available in 3D. If I am not interested in a film, but I'm going along to be social or because my wife is dragging me, 3D isn't a priority.

Now if 3D were the same price as 2D, heck yeah, go 3D. The only people who wouldn't go 3D in a same-price scenario are people with sight/head issues with 3D.

Sadly, 3D TVs are also going away, so the studios are now making 3D BluRays extinct, even when a film was in 3D in the theater!

tl;dr: By trying.

3D has failed twice before. People don't care. It's a gimmick - it's a Disney trick for fifteen minutes and after that all it does is mark the movie for eternity as "made for 3D" whenever some effect flies at the lens.

The one thing that has been proven over and over and over is that people care about a good story, good script, good direction, and good acting. Other things may come and go - some gimmicks may tickle the fancy of the moviegoing public for a season - but good movies are always rooted in the same formula.

And what's so sadly comical is that they are the cheapest things to invest in. Take a look at "He Never Died" or "The Midnight Man" - two low-budget quasi-indie movies I saw this year that I love and have watched over and over. No massive CGI or big-name actors... just half-decent innovative, interesting scripts that are fun to watch.
